courses.title: Foundations of Biology: Energy, Matter, and Information
courses.description: [GE 5B] Using the central lens of evolution, this course will examine the acquisition, utilization, and flow of energy and cycling of matter through the biological hierarchy. The flow of information across different organizational levels and timescales will also be explored. Corequisite(s): BIO 1210L .

courses.title: Foundations of Biology: Energy, Matter, and Information Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Using hands-on activities, students will examine the flow of energy, the cycling of matter, and the flow of information through different timescales and organizational levels of life. Emphasis will be placed on the application of the practices of science. Corequisite(s): BIO 1210 .

courses.title: Foundations of Biology: Evolution, Ecology, and Biodiversity
courses.description: Using the central lens of evolution, this course will examine the reproduction, development, interactions, and adaptations of organisms within their environments. Bacteria, plants, animals, and all other lineages of life, at all levels of biological organization, will be explored. Corequisite(s): BIO 1220L .

courses.title: Foundations of Biology: Evolution, Ecology, and Biodiversity Laboratory
courses.description: Using hands-on activities, including field surveys and dissections, students will examine the diversity of life. Evolutionary and ecological perspectives to life’s biodiversity will be emphasized, as will the application of the practices of science. Corequisite(s): BIO 1220 .

courses.title: Biostatistics Laboratory
courses.description: A laboratory course in the applied statistical analysis of biological research data. Emphasis on performing data analysis using current statistical software, as well as understanding, interpreting, and presenting results of statistical analysis.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L . Pre or Corequisite(s): STA 1300 .

courses.title: Genetics
courses.description: The flow of genetic information involving DNA, RNA and protein. Introduction to patterns of inheritance, transmission (Mendelian) genetics, nuclear structure, mechanisms of gene expression, genomics, molecular genetics and recombinant DNA technology.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Cell and Molecular Biology
courses.description: Cellular processes and molecular interactions, including transport, chemical signaling, cell-cell adhesion, intercellular communication, support and movement, energy conversions, digestion, assembly of macro-molecules and organelles, gene control in prokaryotes and eukaryotes. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2400 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Principles of Evolution
courses.description: A study of biological evolution as a natural process resulting in the generation of biodiversity and ultimately the origin of humans. Overview of the basic principles of scientific knowledge and the history of evolutionary thinking, leading to the development of the modern Theory of Evolution. Review of the origin and history of life on Earth and the fossil record. Analysis of evolutionary processes at the molecular, organismal, and ecosystem levels.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 123/BIO 123L and BIO 303; or BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L and BIO 2400 ; or BIO 122/BIO 122L and BIO 1220C.

courses.title: Principles of Ecology
courses.description: Survey of ecological theory and practice, including interactions between organisms and their abiotic and biotic environment. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L , BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: [GE 5A] Fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including atomic and molecular structure; nomenclature; stoichiometry; solution chemistry, including acid-base and redox chemistry; quantum theory; periodic properties; bonding theory; thermochemistry; gases; and intermolecular forces. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210L .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory experiments to illustrate and enhance lecture topics in CHM 1210 . Basic laboratory techniques and practices. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210 .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: General Chemistry II
courses.description: [GE 5A] Continuation of the development of fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including kinetics; equilibria, including acid-base chemistry; buffers; titrations; thermodynamics; electrochemistry; colligative properties; and nuclear chemistry. Corequisite(s): CHM 1220L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 1210 , CHM 122 or CHM 122B; and C- or better in CHM 1210L , CHM 122L or CHM122LB.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory experiments to illustrate and enhance lecture topics in CHM 1220. Qualitative analysis. Basic laboratory techniques and practices. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): CHM 1220 .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 1210 , CHM 122 or CHM 122B; and C- or better in CHM 1210L , CHM 122L or CHM122LB.

courses.title: Elements of Organic Chemistry
courses.description: The fundamental concepts of organic chemistry will be presented, for students who are required to take one semester of organic chemistry. Topics covered include chemical bonding, molecular structure, stereochemistry, nomenclature, physical properties, thermodynamics and kinetics, acid-base chemistry, organic reaction mechanisms, synthesis and biomolecules. Not open to chemistry majors. Not open to chemistry majors.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; and CHM 123L or CHM 1220L .

courses.title: Elements of Organic Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to general techniques of the organic laboratory for the separation, purification and identification of organic substances. Survey of simple reactions of various functional groups. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; and CHM 123L or CHM 1220L ; or concurrent enrollment in CHM 2010 .

courses.title: Organic Chemistry I
courses.description: Modern concepts of chemical bonding, molecular structure, conformations, nomenclature, thermodynamics and kinetics, acid-base chemistry, stereochemistry, organic reaction intermediates and mechanisms, and synthesis. The physical properties, preparations and reactions of alkanes, haloalkanes, alkenes, alkynes and alcohols.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; and C- or better in CHM 123L or CHM 1220L .

courses.title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: Introduction to synthesis, isolation, purification, and characterization of organic compounds. A focus of this applied learning will be the theory, interpretation, and application of identifying compounds utilizing IR and NMR spectra. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 3140 or CHM 315; CHM 3140 can be concurrent.

courses.title: Elements of Biochemistry
courses.description: Introductory course in biochemistry that surveys the major topics of the discipline; including the structure and functional properties of the biomolecules, and the principles of catabolic metabolism.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 1220 or CHM 122; and C- or better in CHM 315, CHM 201, CHM 2010 , or CHM 3150 .

courses.title: Biochemistry I
courses.description: Biochemistry that systematically covers the topics of biomolecule structure and function. The first semester course of a yearlong course. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement. Corequisite(s): CHM 3270LW .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 1220 , CHM 1220L , CHM 3150 , and CHM 3140L ; D or better in BIO 1150 or BIO 1210 ; and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Stretch Composition II
courses.description: [GE 1A] Review essay structures and rhetorical principles, critical reading, and online research. Introduce disciplinary genres and rhetorical strategies. Frequent practice writing essays, letters, and other genres commonly used in academic writing. Second course in two-course sequence. Sections designated with an M are recommended for multilingual speakers.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in ENG 100, ENG 106, ENG 108, or ENG 1100 .

courses.title: First Year Composition
courses.description: [GE 1A] Principal concepts of rhetoric, argumentation, and research. Frequent practice writing essays, letters, and other genres commonly used in academic writing. Sections designated with an M are recommended for multilingual speakers.
courses.prerequisites: CO Category II.

courses.title: Written Reasoning
courses.description: [GE 1B] Inquiry into written reasoning in actual rhetorical situations. Analysis of relations among logical claims, lines of reasoning, interpretation of evidence, and the judgment of these by audiences. Papers and critical reading of non-fiction argumentation.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1A/A2.

courses.title: Critical Thinking
courses.description: [GE 1B] Examination of formal and informal reasoning processes in everyday and scientific reasoning; emphasis on detection and avoidance of informal fallacies with examples from contemporary social issues.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: [GE 2] Functions, limits, continuity, derivatives of all functions including trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, inverse trigonometric, and implicit functions. Applications of derivatives, including max/min problems and L’Hopitals rule. Definite and Indefinite Integrals, The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, substitution rule and applications.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1050 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1052 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1055 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1070 ; AP PreCalculus >=3; or ALEKS Comp >=76.

courses.title: Calculus for Life Sciences
courses.description: [GE 2] Concepts of functions and the idea of change. Review of algebraic, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions. Brief review of fundamental topics in right triangle trigonometry. Graphing, limits, derivatives, differentials, and integrals of single variable functions listed above. Optimization problems and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. Special emphasis is given to applications in life sciences.
courses.prerequisites: AP PreCalculus >=3, ALEKS Comp >=61, C or better in MAT 1050 , C or better in MAT 1052 , C or better in MAT 1055 , or C or better in MAT 1070 .

courses.title: Physics of Motion, Fluids, and Heat
courses.description: [GE 5A] Introduction to Newtonian mechanics and thermodynamics: Kinematics, forces, conservation laws, viscous fluids, heat transfer, and the microscopic nature of gases. Emphasis on biological applications. Corequisite(s): PHY 1210L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 106, MAT 1060 , MAT 112, MAT 114, MAT 1140 , MAT 1140C, MAT 115, MAT 116, MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , or MAT 1300 . ( MAT 1300 can be concurrent.)

courses.title: Physics of Motion, Fluids, and Heat Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Experiments on Newtonian mechanics, fluids, and heat. Corequisite(s): PHY 1210 .

courses.title: Physics of Electromagnetism, Circuits, and Light
courses.description: Electric and magnetic forces and fields, DC and AC circuits, oscillations, electromagnetic waves, optics, and analogies between diffusion and electrostatics. Corequisite(s): PHY 1220L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in PHY 122, PHY 122B, PHY 1210 , or PHY 1210B.

courses.title: Electromagnetism, Circuits, and Light Laboratory
courses.description: Experiments on electromagnetism, oscillations, and optics. Corequisite(s): PHY 1220 .

courses.title: Introduction to Newtonian Mechanics
courses.description: [GE 5A] Introduction to mechanics, including Newton’s laws, vectors, statics, kinematics, conservation laws, rotational motion, Newtonian gravity, fluids, and simple harmonic motion. Corequisite(s): PHY 1510L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 114, MAT 1140 , MAT 1140C, MAT 115, MAT 116 or MAT 1150 ( MAT 1150 can be concurrent).

courses.title: Newtonian Mechanics Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Experiments in Newtonian mechanics. Corequisite(s): PHY 1510 .

courses.title: Introduction to Electromagnetism and Circuits
courses.description: Introduction to electricity and magnetism, including electrostatics, dc circuits, magnetostatics, electrodynamics, and Maxwell’s equations. Corequisite(s): PHY 1520L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 115 or MAT 1150 ; and C- or better in PHY 132, PHY 132B, PHY 1510B or PHY 1510 .

courses.title: Introductory Laboratory on Electromagnetism and Circuits
courses.description: Experiments in electricity and magnetism. Corequisite(s): PHY 1520 .

courses.title: Biostatistics
courses.description: [GE 2] Basic definitions, Sampling methods, Graphical display and descriptive statistics. Probability concepts, Normal distribution. Estimation, hypothesis testing, t-tests, goodness of fit, analysis of variance, regression and correlation, and nonparametric procedures. Applications in biological, agricultural, and other applied science. Use of computer packages for applied problems.
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, MDPT >=14, ALEKS >=46, SAT >=570, ACT >=23, C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course, or C- or better or CR in MAT 1051 .

courses.title: Form and Function in Plants
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 8 units
courses.description: The interplay between the anatomy and morphology of green plants and their physiology. The anatomical and physiological bases of development, growth regulation, water relations, reproduction, and the production and transport of food. Corequisite(s): BIO 2050L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Form and Function in Plants Laboratory
courses.description: Investigations of the anatomy, morphology, physiology, reproduction, and phylogeny of green plants. Emphasis is place on the exploration of the function and arrangement of tissues in organs, the major photosynthetic strategies, the effects of the environment on plant water relations, and the relationship between life cycles and the green plant phylogeny. Corequisite(s): BIO 2050 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Basic Microbiology
courses.description: A study of cell structure, function, metabolism, genetics, and diversity of microorganisms. The impacts of microorganisms on evolutionary, environmental and disease processes are discussed. Corequisite(s): BIO 2060L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Basic Microbiology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory techniques and methods used to study of cell structure, function, metabolism, genetics, and diversity of microorganisms. Identification and growth of microorganisms, as well as scientific thinking, are emphasized in the laboratory exercises. Corequisite(s): BIO 2060 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Introduction to Invertebrate Zoology
courses.description: Introduction to the biology of invertebrates. Selected aspects of invertebrate evolution, phylogenetics, feeding, respiration, water balance, reproduction, internal coordination, locomotion, and development will be covered. Corequisite(s): BIO 2370L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 121/BIO 121L, BIO 122/BIO 122L, and BIO 123/BIO 123L; BIO 121/BIO 121L and BIO 122/BIO 122L/BIO 1220C; BIO 121/BIO 121L/BIO 1210B and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; BIO 115/115L/115A; or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Introduction to Invertebrate Zoology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory-based introduction to the biology of invertebrates. Emphasis is placed on the evolution of body plans, form/function relationships from cells to organ system levels, and natural history of invertebrates. Dissections of selected invertebrate taxa highlight major differences among major invertebrate lineages. Corequisite(s): BIO 2370 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 121/BIO 121L, BIO 122/BIO 122L, and BIO 123/BIO 123L; BIO 121/BIO 121L and BIO 122/BIO 122L/BIO 1220C; BIO 121/BIO 121L/BIO 1210B and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; BIO 115/115L/115A; or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Introduction to Vertebrate Zoology
courses.description: Introduction to the evolution, phylogenetics, anatomy, physiology, and natural history of vertebrates. Corequisite(s): BIO 2380L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 121/BIO 121L, BIO 122/BIO 122L, and BIO 123/BIO 123L; BIO 121/BIO 121L and BIO 122/BIO 122L/BIO 1220C; BIO 121/BIO 121L/BIO 1210B and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; BIO 115/115L/115A; or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Introduction to Vertebrate Zoology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory-based introduction to the biology of vertebrates. Emphasis is placed on morphological evolution, form/function relationships from tissue to whole-animal levels. Dissections of select vertebrate taxa to examine organ systems, their structure and function, and their evolutionary homologies. Corequisite(s): BIO 2380 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 121/BIO 121L, BIO 122/BIO 122L, and BIO 123/BIO 123L; BIO 121/BIO 121L and BIO 122/BIO 122L/BIO 1220C; BIO 121/BIO 121L/BIO 1210B and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; BIO 115/115L/115A; or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Physiology I: Cells
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: Principles of physiological mechanisms at the cellular level including the macromolecular assembly of cellular structure, membrane structure and transport processes, electrical and chemical signaling, and protein interactions. Corequisite(s): BIO 4450L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 310 or BIO 3220W .

courses.title: Physiology I: Cells Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory-based introduction to the study of physiological mechanisms at the cellular level. Knowledge and experience of using practical methods to study the macromolecular assembly of cellular structure, membrane structure and transport processes, electrical and chemical signaling, and protein interactions. Corequisite(s): BIO 4450 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 310 or BIO 3220W .

courses.title: Physiology II: Systems
courses.description: Principles of integrative physiology presented through an organ-system approach. Cellular and molecular mechanisms also discussed to provide current views of physiological processes. Emphasis on mammals, but other vertebrate taxa also covered to highlight fundamental themes.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 310 or BIO 3220W .

courses.title: Plant Physiology
courses.description: An overview of physiological processes in plants including water relations, soils, mineral nutrition, photosynthesis, and responses to environmental (biotic and abiotic) influences on plant growth. In depth examination of how environmental signals are processed via hormones in controlling gene expression and plant development. Corequisite(s): BIO 4480L .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L, or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Plant Physiology Laboratory
courses.description: Inquiry-based laboratory exercises involving plant water relations, enzyme isolation and analysis, aseptic culture of plant material, mineral deficiencies, enzyme activity in germination and later development of tissues, as well as photoperiodism and hormonal influences on plant growth and development. Corequisite(s): BIO 4480 .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L, or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Microbial Physiology
courses.description: Life processes of prokaryotic microorganisms. The diverse nutritional requirements and metabolism exhibited by microorganisms, growth, structure and function relationships, and genetic control.
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L , and CHM 201/CHM 250L or CHM 3140 / CHM 3140L .

courses.title: Microbial Physiology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory techniques and methods used to study life processes of prokaryotic microorganisms: nutrition, growth, metabolism, structure and function, and genetic control.
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L , and CHM 201/CHM 250 or CHM 3140 / CHM 3140L . Pre or Corequisite(s): BIO 4660 .

courses.title: Genetics and Human Issues
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3 units
courses.description: [GE 5D] Nontechnical introduction to genetic principles with emphasis on humans. Topics include hereditary diseases; gene structure, function and regulation; genetic engineering; human genome; cancer; cloning; genetic technologies in medicine; forensics, and agriculture; genetic fingerprinting, ethical and social issues. For non-biology majors.May be used as approved elective, but not for required upper division credit by students with majors in the Biological Sciences Department.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Sexually Transmitted Diseases and Safer Sex
courses.description: [GE 5D] An overview of the biology of sexually-transmitted diseases (STD), including AIDS and the impact these diseases and current therapies have on society at large. Topics include distribution, transmission, sexual practices, effect on immune system, treatments, prevention, testing and counseling. May be used as approved elective, but not for required upper division credit by students with majors in the Biological Sciences Department.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Environment and Society
courses.description: [GE 5D] Environmental problems related to use of natural resources by modern societies. Issues discussed include availability of food, water, and energy by a rapidly growing world population, and the effects of pollution, climate change and decreasing biodiversity on ecosystems and societies. May be used as approved elective, but not for required upper division credit by students with majors in the Biological Sciences Department.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Biodiversity Conservation
courses.description: [GE 5D] Course addresses global patterns of biological diversity, the impact of humans on natural systems and diversity, and use of scientific principles to protect and restore diversity. Open to all majors. May be used as approved elective, but not for required upper division credit by students with majors in the Biological Sciences Department.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Marine Biology
courses.description: [GE 5D] An overview of the marine physical environment and the organisms that inhabit it. Emphasis on the interconnections between the ecology of the oceans and the rest of the biosphere, including human activities. May be used as approved elective, but not for required upper division credit by students with majors in the Biological Sciences Department.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Biology of Aging
courses.description: [GE 5D] The physiology of aging, age-related diseases, biological basis of aging processes and aging intervention. Topics include basic physiological changes and chronic diseases associated with biological aging, aging theories, biomarkers used to measure biological aging, cellular signaling pathways linked with aging process, stem cells and aging, genetic and environmental impacts on aging, and aging intervention drugs and nutraceuticals. Primary literatures on these topics will be utilized to help students synthesize acquired knowledge on aging and apply that to real life decision-making, develop critical thinking in analyzing aging related information, and contribute to the broader discussion on the inter-relationships between aging manipulation, human population and environmental sustainability. May be used as approved elective support, but not for upper division core credit by students with majors in the Biological Sciences Department.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Evolution of Plants Laboratory
courses.description: The evolution of plants will be investigated through the comparative morphology, life cycles, and other reproductive patterns of the green plants. Methods will include observations of fossils, live, and preserved specimens. Corequisite(s): BIO 4520 .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L and BIO 413; or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L and BIO 3240 .

courses.title: Plant Genetics
courses.description: Principles and processes in classical and modern plant genetics. Topics include Mendelian genetics, gene regulation, genome architecture and evolution, and plant genomics.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 121/BIO 121L, BIO 122/BIO 122L, and BIO 123/BIO 123L; BIO 121/BIO 121L and BIO 122/BIO122L/BIO 1220C; BIO 121/BIO 121L/BIO 1210B and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; or BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L . BIO 2400 and BIO 2050 recommended.

courses.title: Plants and the Environment
courses.description: Study of the interrelationships between plants and their environment with an emphasis on the response of plant species, populations, communities, and ecosystems to changing abiotic and biotic conditions. Corequisite(s): BIO 4570L .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201, BOT 201L, BIO 211L, BIO 325 and BIO 325L; or BIO 2050 , BIO 2050L , BIO 2110L , BIO 3250W and BIO 3250LW .

courses.title: Plants and the Environment Laboratory
courses.description: Application of field and laboratory techniques used by plant ecologists to study physiology, populations, communities, and ecosystems. Corequisite(s): BIO 4570 .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/201L BIO 211L and BIO 325/325L, or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L , BIO 2110L and BIO 3250W / BIO 3250LW .

courses.title: Marine Botany
courses.description: Evolution, development, reproduction, morphology, taxonomy, physiology, and ecology of marine algae. A focus is placed on the identification and study of local species. Corequisite(s): BIO 4490L .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L, or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Marine Botany Laboratory
courses.description: Field and laboratory investigations of marine algae. A focus is placed on the identification and study of local species, including experiences in experimental design, field research, data analyses, and scientific writing. Weekend field trips are required. Weekend field trips are required. Weekend field trips are required. Corequisite(s): BIO 4490 .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L, or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L .

courses.title: California Flora
courses.description: Introduction to the plant communities of California and their dominant species, with special attention given to those in the California Floristic Province. Botanical terminology used in dichotomous keys and identification books and online resources will be explained, along with descriptions of the major plant families of California in terms of their vegetative and floral characteristics. Corequisite(s): BIO 4500L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: California Flora Laboratory
courses.description: Identification of California wild land plants using dichotomous keys and other resources. Recognition of common plant families. Overview of the geographic distribution of plants in southern California. Corequisite(s): BIO 4500 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Plant Anatomy
courses.description: Origin, development, and characteristics of cells, tissues, and tissue systems in the roots, stems, and leaves of vascular plants. Corequisite(s): BIO 4530L .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Plant Anatomy Laboratory
courses.description: Microscopic study of representative plants concerning the origin, development, and characteristics of cells, tissues, and tissue systems in the roots, stems, and leaves of vascular plants. Corequisite(s): BIO 4530 .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Field Biology
courses.description: Dual Listed as: BIO 5550 Group study of a selected topic in Field Biology for upper-division and graduate students. Course title and number of units are specified in advance. Students receive credit for multiple courses with the BIO 4550 or BIO 5550 designation if course topics are different. Corequisite(s): Special topics course requisites added as needed.
courses.prerequisites: Special topics course requisites added as needed.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics

courses.title: Field Biology Laboratory
courses.description: Dual Listed as: BIO 5550L Laboratory study of a selected topic in Field Biology for upper-division students and graduate students. Course topic and number of units are specified in advance. Students receive credit for multiple courses with the BIO 4550L or BIO 5550L designation if course topics are different. Corequisite(s): Special topics course requisites added as needed.
courses.prerequisites: Special topics course requisites added as needed.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics

courses.title: Plant Development and Differentiation
courses.description: The role of external and internal cues such as hormones, temperature, signaling in germination, growth and reproduction of plants. Advanced topics such floral biology including pollination and floral development will also be covered.
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L, or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Entomology
courses.description: Insect structure and function, evolution, growth and development, behavior, ecology, and influence on human societies; includes a survey of the major insect groups.
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing and any 2000 level BIO course.

courses.title: Entomology Laboratory
courses.description: Primary focus is on the identification/ classification and natural history of common Insect Orders and Families. A group field project that involves insect sampling and quantitative analysis of samples is required. The field project may be used to satisfy the departmental capstone requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing and any 2000 level BIO course.

courses.title: Developmental Biology
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Explore how animals develop from a single cell into a complex organism with a focus on the genetic, cellular, and molecular mechanisms controlling development. Using a model systems approach, topics in pattern formation and organ development will be discussed. Also covered will be topics related to developmental defects, diseases, and tissue regeneration.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 310 or BIO 3220W .

courses.title: Human Genetics
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Single and multi-gene human diseases, chromosomal aberrations, sex determination, immunogenetics, genetic counseling and genomics. Problem-solving and mastering concepts of medical and biochemical genetics.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 310 or BIO 3220W .

courses.title: Advanced Genetics
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Recent advances in genetics with emphasis on methods of gene investigation, and manipulation using molecular, quantitative, and whole genome methods.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2400 or BIO 303.

courses.title: Regulatory Affairs and Safety Assessment
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Examination of laws and regulations governing biological products, such as foods and drugs, and the environment. Approaches and toxicology methods to determine safety of biological products and compounds in the environment. Concepts in risk assessment. Culmination of material through capstone project.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 123/BIO 123L, BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 122/BIO 122L/BIO 1220C, or Instructor consent.

courses.title: Genetic Engineering - Past, Present and Future
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Dual Listed as: BIO 5170 Covers the major milestone discoveries and related anecdotes in the history of genetic engineering technologies, the major applications of these technologies in agriculture, biotech and medicine, and how technologies might evolve in the future based on current cutting-edge development. From the first genetically engineered human drug, synthetic insulin, to converting a human skin cell into an egg or sperm cell, exploring the principles, the scientists and intriguing events, the social and environmental implications and the ethics behind each technology, as well as how future technologies could transform humanity.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 3220W .

courses.title: Concepts of Molecular Biology
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: The molecular basis and control mechanisms of biological processes such as DNA replication, DNA recombination and DNA transposition, transcription and translation. Will provide an understanding of diverse signal transduction pathways regulating and regulated by gene expression.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 310 or BIO 3220W .

courses.title: Molecular Biology Techniques
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Theory of major techniques currently used in the isolation and analysis of nucleic acids and proteins. Emphasis is placed on the scientific principles behind contemporary techniques such as chromatography, electrophoresis, PCR, DNA sequencing and analysis, and the specific application of these techniques to basic and applied research.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 310 or BIO 3220W .

courses.title: Molecular Biology Techniques Laboratory
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Hands-on experience with major techniques currently used in the isolation and analysis of proteins and nucleic acids. Emphasis is placed on column chromatography, gel electrophoresis, reverse-transcriptase-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and centrifugation techniques.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 310 or BIO 3220W . Pre or Corequisite(s): BIO 4320 .

courses.title: Recombinant DNA and Protein Technology
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Proteins control almost every aspect of cellular functions. The study of proteins and their functions is central to understand the regulation of cells and organs. Coverage of the knowledge about recombinant DNA and protein technologies and discusses their applications. Corequisite(s): BIO 4360L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 3220W .

courses.title: Recombinant DNA and Protein Technology Laboratory
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Hands-on experience with major techniques currently used in recombinant protein production. This includes cDNA amplification, restriction enzyme digestion, ligation, transformation, colony screening, sequencing data analysis, protein expression, purification, characterization, and use of recombinant protein in cell biology studies.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 3220W . Pre or Corequisite(s): BIO 4360 .

courses.title: Bioinformatics
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: A survey of computational techniques and software applications currently used to organize, manipulate, and explore biological information. Students learn the theoretical bases of modern bioinformatic analysis. Some of the topics covered include sequence alignment, biological databases, phylogenetic reconstruction, analysis of protein structure and function. Corequisite(s): BIO 4380L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 303, BIO 2400 , CHM 328, or CHM 3280 .

courses.title: Bioinformatics Laboratory
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Practice with methods used in modern bioinformatics for the manipulation and analysis of large scale molecular data sets using computer based methods. Some of the topics covered include, pairwise and multiple sequence alignment, pattern searching in biological databases, and high throughput data analysis and manipulation. This is a hands-on course focused on developing practical bioinformatics skills. Corequisite(s): BIO 4380 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 303, BIO 2400 , CHM 328, or CHM 3280 .

courses.title: Tissue Culture and Its Application
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Principles of animal cell culture in laboratory setting and the applications of animal tissue culture to studies in cell biology and biotechnology. Topics include tissue culture basics; tissue culture lab setting, equipment and safety; tissue culture media and supplements; biology of cultured cells; subculture and cell lines; cloning and selection; cell characterization; contamination management.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 3220W .

courses.title: Tissue Culture and Its Application Laboratory
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Hands-on experience with basic techniques currently used in the culturing of animal cells, including tissue culture, subculture, cell storage, transfection of cells, synchronizing cells, analyzing cells and fluorescence microscopy.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 3220W . Pre or Corequisite(s): BIO 4430 .

courses.title: Stem Cell Biology
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: An overview of current stem cell research and its potential applications in regenerative medicine and chemical toxicity tests. Topics include mammalian embryo development; mouse and human embryonic stem cells; induced pluripotent stem cells; human adult stem cells; cancer stem cells and plant stem cells.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 310 or BIO 3220W .

courses.title: Stem Cell Biology Laboratory
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Hands-on practice with basic cell culture will include: Basic cell culture techniques, culture and differentiation of human adult stem cells, characterization of differentiated mature osteocytes and adipocytes, human pluripotent stem cell culture (differentiation and characterization), and In vitro genetic manipulation in live cells. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 310 or BIO 3220W . Pre or Corequisite(s): BIO 4400 .

courses.title: Organic Chemistry II
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: The study of the properties, synthesis and reactions of alcohols, ethers, aldehydes, ketones, enols and enolates, carboxylic acids, carboxylic acid derivatives, conjugated systems, aromatic compounds, amines. Special topics include advanced synthetic strategies, biomolecules, and polymers.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 3140 , CHM 315, or CHM 315B.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: The principles of synthesis, characterization isolation, purification, and characterization of organic compounds. A focus of this applied learning will be the theory, interpretation, and application of identifying compounds utilizing IR, NMR, Mass Spectroscopy. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 3140L or CHM 318L; and CHM 316 or CHM 3150 . Pre or Corequisite(s): CHM 3150 .

courses.title: Biochemistry II
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Biochemistry that focuses on the topics of anabolic and catabolic metabolism, the regulation of metabolism, enzyme mechanisms, and cofactors. The second semester course of a yearlong course.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 328 or CHM 3270W , and C- or better in CHM 328L or CHM 3270LW .

courses.title: Biochemistry Laboratory II
courses.requirement: Emphasis 2 - Cell and Molecular Biology+: 16 units
courses.description: Experimental biochemistry that systematically covers protein purification, biomolecular assays, thermodynamics, and bioinformatics. The second semester course of a yearlong course.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 328 or CHM 3270W , and C- or better in CHM 328L or CHM 3270LW .

courses.title: Applied Microbiology
courses.description: Industrial and applied uses of microorganisms. Emphasis on utilization of microbes for food production and processing, water and sewage treatment, healthcare products, biotechnology and bioremediation. Corequisite(s): BIO 3620L .
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L ; CHM 201 or CHM 3150 ; and CHM 250L, CHM 2010L , CHM 317L, or CHM 3140L .

courses.title: Applied Microbiology Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on experience with applied uses of microorganisms. Emphasis on methods for examining microbes, microbial products or microbial action important in food production and processing, water and sewage treatment and analysis, control of microbes, healthcare products, biotechnology and bioremediation. Corequisite(s): BIO 3620 .
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L ; CHM 201 or CHM 3150 ; and CHM 250L, CHM 2010L , CHM 317L, or CHM 3140L .

courses.title: Food Microbiology
courses.description: Cross Listed as: FST 3640 A study of the roles of microorganisms in food spoilage, foodborne illness, and fermentation. Factors that influence microbial growth in food and how the growth can be controlled are discussed.
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L .

courses.title: Food Microbiology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory techniques and methods used to study of microorganisms in food. Analysis and detection of foodborne microorganisms using cultural and molecular techniques. Scientific thinking and quantitative analysis are emphasized through each laboratory exercise and a term project.
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L . Pre or Corequisite(s): BIO 3640 .

courses.title: Medical Microbiology
courses.description: The pathogenesis of bacterial and fungal infections with an emphasis on morphological, biochemical, and virulence factors associated with host susceptibility to infection, laboratory methods of diagnosis and available treatment and prevention options.
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L .

courses.title: Medical Microbiology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory techniques and methods used to study the pathogenesis of bacterial and fungal infections. Identification and growth of microorganisms, as well as scientific thinking, are emphasized in the laboratory exercises. Corequisite(s): BIO 4635 .
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L .

courses.title: Immunology
courses.description: Dual Listed as: BIO 5650 Principles of serology and immunology with an emphasis on immune mechanisms at the molecular and cellular level. Topics include innate and adaptive immune responses, immune cells and organs, production and activity of cytokines, antibodies, and complement.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2060 and BIO 2060L . Pre or Corequisite(s): BIO 3220W .

courses.title: Immunology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory techniques and methods used to study principles of serology and immunology with an emphasis on immune mechanisms at the molecular and cellular level. Production of antibodies, testing of produced antibodies, identification and function of immune cells and their by-products including cytokines, as well as scientific thinking, are emphasized in the laboratory exercises. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L . Pre or Corequisite(s): BIO 4650 or MIC 415.

courses.title: General Virology
courses.description: Examination of the nature, structure and classification of viruses and their infectious cycle as intracellular parasites; learning the basics of how viruses are transmitted, how they cause diseases and strategies to prevent viral infections. Various types of viral vaccines, the relationship between virus and cancer, virus evolution, emerging viruses, antiviral drug development, and unusual infectious agents such as prions will also be discussed. Corequisite(s): BIO 4670L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 2060 . Pre or Corequisite(s): BIO 3220.

courses.title: General Virology Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on experience with basic techniques currently used for cultivating and assaying viruses. This includes plaque assay, virus growth curve determination, identification of virus from environment, characterization of virus by gel electrophoresis, detection of virus by PCR and ELISA, culture animal viruses in chicken embryos and animal tissue culture, etc. Corequisite(s): BIO 4670 .
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 .

courses.title: Microbial Ecology
courses.description: Examination of microorganisms in their natural environments, microbe-microbe interactions, microbe-virus interactions, cell-to-cell communication mechanisms, and methods of microbial analysis in natural environments. Microbial roles in biogeochemical cycling, ecosystem functioning, industrial, agricultural, and environmental applications will be studied.
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L .

courses.title: Microbial Ecology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory reinforces the principles and provides exposure to methods used in microbial ecology with a special emphasis on molecular approaches.
courses.prerequisites: MIC 201/MIC 201L or BIO 2060 / BIO 2060L . Pre or Corequisite(s): BIO 4680 .

courses.title: Hematology
courses.description: The study of human blood with an emphasis on the anatomy and physiology of the normal and abnormal hematopoietic systems, including hemostasis and related diseases. Capstone experience includes problem solving using patient cases.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 121/BIO 121L, BIO 122/BIO 122L, and BIO 123/BIO 123L; BIO 121/BIO 121L and BIO 122/BIO122L/BIO 1220C; BIO 121/BIO 121L/BIO 1210B and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; or BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L .

courses.title: Hematology Laboratory
courses.description: Practice performing common hematological laboratory procedures including direct blood typing, indirect blood typing, irregular antibody detection, DAT, IAT, cross matching, donor selection and quality control. Students are also required to identify the morphology of different form cell elements in both normal and abnormal blood smears, including performing CBC.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 121/BIO 121L, BIO 122/BIO 122L, and BIO 123/BIO 123L; BIO 121/BIO 121L and BIO 122/BIO122L/BIO 1220C; BIO 121/BIO 121L/BIO 1210B and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; or BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L . Pre or Corequisite(s): BIO 4700 .

courses.title: Biophysics
courses.description: Cross Listed as: PHY 4100 A quantitative exploration of biological systems and the physical mechanisms underlying their operation. Topics may include membrane physics, the relationship between blood flow and metabolic scaling laws, diffusion and random walks, and a unified treatment of heat, fluid, solute, and electrical transport in biological systems.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in PHY 123, PHY 1220 , PHY 133 or PHY 1520 .

courses.title: Neuromuscular Physiology
courses.description: In depth study of the molecular, structural, and functional mechanisms associated with the neuromuscular unit, including the motor system and skeletal muscle, and cellular and molecular processes associated with adaptation of the neuromuscular unit to a variety of conditions.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 428/BIO 428L or BIO 4450 / BIO 4450L .

courses.title: Neuroscience
courses.description: The properties of ion channels, transporters, and the principles of electrical excitability. Synaptic structure, storing, and transmitting information. The birth, survival, death, and migration of neurons during development and during adulthood. An introduction to the biology of the senses with an emphasis on a systems level perspective. General topics include the tactile, visual, olfactory, auditory, gustatory, somatic motor, and visceromotor systems as well as nociception.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 3220W .

courses.title: Biology of Species Invasions
courses.description: Biological and ecological foundations for the increasingly serious threat of invasive species to native ecosystems and human economies and health. Corequisite(s): BIO 4140A .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 123/BIO 123L, BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , BIO 122/BIO 122L/BIO 1220C, BIO 115/BIO 115L/BIO 115A, BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L , BIO 110/BIO 111L, or BIO 1110 / BIO 1110L .

courses.title: Biology of Species Invasions Activity
courses.description: Discussion and analysis of primary literature on the biological and ecological impacts of invasive and non-native species to native ecosystems and human economies and health. Oral presentations and group discussion of papers emphasized. Corequisite(s): BIO 4140 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 , BIO 1210L , BIO 1220 , BIO 1220L , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Marine Ecology
courses.description: Structure and function of marine ecosystems with emphasis on coastal ecosystems, such as kelp forests, estuaries, and rocky intertidal ecosystems. Understanding abiotic and biotic processes and how these relate to the distribution and biology of animals and plants. Corequisite(s): BIO 4180L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 325/BIO 325L or BIO 3250W .

courses.title: Marine Ecology Laboratory
courses.description: Field and laboratory investigations of the structure and function of marine ecosystems with emphasis on coastal ecosystems. Experience in experimental design, field research, data analyses, and scientific writing. Weekend field trips are required. Corequisite(s): BIO 4180 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 325/BIO 325L or BIO 3250W .

courses.title: Ecotoxicology
courses.description: How to think critically about pollutants in the environment - how they interact with biological systems, and how they affect individuals, populations, communities, ecosystems, and our society. Promoting an understanding of: the scientific process for investigating the effects of toxicants on biological systems; the major types and sources of contamination, including environmental disasters; how biological systems and society are affected by, and respond to the issues that pollutants create.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 and BIO 1220 .

courses.title: Biology of Fishes
courses.description: The structure, relationships, classification, general biology and zoogeography of fishes. Corequisite(s): BIO 4820L .
courses.prerequisites: Any 2000-level BIO course or junior standing.

courses.title: Biology of Fishes Laboratory
courses.description: The structure, relationships, classification, general biology and zoogeography of fishes. Course includes collection, identification, and field study of local species, and laboratory work with preserved and living material. Weekend field trips are required. Corequisite(s): BIO 4820 .
courses.prerequisites: Any 2000-level BIO course or junior standing.

courses.title: Ornithology
courses.description: An understanding of the ecology, evolution, and diversification of birds, with particular relevance for North American birds. The range of physiological, anatomical, and behavioral adaptations that allow birds to live in ecosystems across our entire planet. Consistent with the historical and current fundamental role of birds in science, emphasizing birds’ importance to scientific discovery, knowledge of the world, and our society. The course will also strive to inspire students’ curiosity and awe for the diversity of birds, their adaptations and ecological roles, their beautiful appearances, their songs, and their many extraordinary abilities. Corequisite(s): BIO 4830L .
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing and any 2000-level BIO course.

courses.title: Ornithology Laboratory
courses.description: Identification of North American birds, while developing an understanding of the techniques used in the scientific study of birds in the field. Identification skills will be cultivated through the use of an instructional collection of bird specimens, and training in the identification of birds in the field based on visual observations and recognition of songs. Corequisite(s): BIO 4830 .
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing and any 2000-level BIO course.

courses.title: Herpetology
courses.description: Evolution, morphology, classification, distribution, ecology, behavior, and conservation of amphibians and reptiles Corequisite(s): BIO 4840L .
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing and any 2000-level BIO course.

courses.title: Herpetology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory study and field investigations of local species of amphibians and reptiles. Diversity, natural history, and methods of observation, capture, handling, and identification are emphasized. Corequisite(s): BIO 4840 .
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing and any 2000-level BIO course.

courses.title: Mammalogy
courses.description: Examines the structure, relationships, classification, general biology, and zoogeography of mammals. Corequisite(s): BIO 4850L .
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing and any 2000-level BIO course.

courses.title: Mammalogy Laboratory
courses.description: Examines the structure, relationships, classification, general biology, and zoogeography of mammals. Laboratory course work includes the examination of mammal skulls, skins, and other preserved specimens, as well as the field study of local species. Weekend field trips are required. Corequisite(s): BIO 4850 .
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing and any 2000-level BIO course.

courses.title: Life Science for Elementary Educators
courses.description: [GE 5B] Introduction to life science, including biological processes (from molecules to ecosystems), the relationship between form and function, reproduction, heredity, evolution, and impact of humans on other organisms. Introduction to modeling effective K-8 curriculum and teaching and assessment practices as described in the state adopted framework and content standards. Corequisite(s): BIO 2120L .

courses.title: Life Science for Elementary Educators Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Inquiry-based, hands on activities and investigations of biological processes from molecules to ecosystems, relationship between form and function, reproduction, heredity, evolution, and the impact of humans on other organisms. Modeling of effective K-8 curriculum, teaching and assessment practices as described in the state adopted framework and content standards. Lecture and lab are integrated closely modeling elementary science teaching. Corequisite(s): BIO 2120 .

courses.title: Special Topics for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Group study at an advanced level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Undergraduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
